request.state: A draft language has isolated single-operation example tables, dependency-closed fixture recipes and simultaneous path selectors evaluated against untouched initial setup. Production deliveries are protected typed handles bound to one canonical operation and storage owner. A test delivery recipe authors only a complete normalized request plus initial status/result/error; owner, principal, binding, ID and revision come from the runner. Five transport snapshots share the same request: pending/null/null, succeeded/declared result/null, failed/null/closed safe error, unknown/null/null-or-safe-error, skipped/null/null. File-valued successful results still require the existing receiving-owner, operation/delivery/result-path finalization and attachment provenance; a file ID, foreign upload or fabricated file object is insufficient. Current selectors patch model initial snapshots but forbid receipt recipe attributes. Existing examples repeat five or six complete requests only to vary initial envelope. Required outcome: all independently authored expected observations and legal-envelope checks remain, without live sends, production receipt writes, new constructors, inheritance or a test operation. Prototype compatibility is not required. This generic brief has no source files, real records or secrets.

fixture_contract.instructions: Choose the smallest coherent draft contract using the same safety, complete evidence, authoring efficiency and evaluation-order criteria; preserve uncertainty about implementation work.

criteria.separate_recipes: Keep a distinct complete operation-resolved recipe for every status/result/error envelope. Existing type/provenance rules and straightforward dependency order remain; repeated request text and recipe declarations stay explicit. No new selector semantics.
criteria.initial_selectors: Allow only direct named-delivery-recipe status, result and error selectors in isolated table setup. Evaluate all cells on immutable untouched setup, reject overlapping/aliased/protected paths, fold the three attributes simultaneously into the full normalized recipe plan, validate the entire envelope and final file provenance, then provision that row's protected receipt once. Keep request, target, identity, principal and ownership fixed. A stored association path or later sequence cannot edit a receipt. Removes per-status declarations but adds an explicit pre-provisioning planning distinction.
criteria.factor_existing_fields: Keep separate complete recipes, but fill their request fields from already-needed readable frozen model fields or named message values where available. This can reduce repeated literal content with no receipt-selector extension, yet repeats recipe shapes, may create dependency cycles when the model points back to the receipt, and offers no universal typed value fixture.
